findings.title: The end step's dirty-tree sentence says an external launch falls to the paste route; the launch route refuses and writes nothing
findings.recommendation: The walk's F2 edit added to CHAIN_END_STEP: "on an uncommitted one the pair refuses and an external launch falls to the paste route, neither writes a run record". The external handoff's Step 3a (review.ts:497, the generated references/external-handoff.md:55) says the opposite for a reachable runner: a dirty tree means "do NOT launch and write NOTHING (no prompt file, no T0)" and print `Not launched: …`. The chain's conclusion holds either way (no run record, so `no-progress`), but the five bodies carrying the end step now state a fallback the handoff never takes, so an AI reading it would expect a paste snippet that is not printed. Reword to "on an uncommitted one the pair and a launched external review both refuse and write nothing, so the chain stops on `no-progress`", re-record the five bodies' hashes, and check the delta (specs/orbit-conventions/spec.md:22-24) and docs/customization.md, which state it correctly already.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T18-10-03Z.json: reader row 4 (decided) — "every other question stops the run" drops D-sc-12's target prompt, which never fires
findings.recommendation: Replace with a record naming all three kinds: a which-change/which-mode question is not asked, a routine one takes its default, every other one stops the run; say the archive cases land with the stage's second change (D-sc-19).

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T18-17-24Z.json: reader row 3 (decided) — "reviews it does itself" does not say whether a fresh review counts

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T18-17-24Z.json: reader row 1 (decided) — "half of a pair" is undefined
findings.recommendation: Define a blind pair (one fresh and one outside review run together) or add it to defines.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T21-50-02Z.json: reader row 3 (decided) — "a finding nobody can settle yet" is vague
findings.recommendation: Say a finding no edit inside the change can fix, whose alternatives the user must choose between.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T21-50-03Z.json: reader row 1 (why) — "launch note" is undefined
findings.recommendation: Say "the record a launch writes before the review runs".

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T21-50-03Z.json: reader row 3 (alternatives/why) — "progress" is not tied to D-sc-14's new-record test, so the loop is unexplained
findings.recommendation: Say progress means a new record on the change's trail since the last run, so a failed launch's own record would let it relaunch forever.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T21-50-04Z.json: reader row 3 (why) — "recorded without being asked" makes the reader reconstruct an unasked stop
findings.recommendation: Say a stop written when nobody was asked has no answer until the user is asked.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T22-12-40Z.json: reader row 3 (decided) — reads as one bad entry turning off the whole setting; only that entry grants nothing
findings.recommendation: Say an entry whose value is not true grants nothing, the other entries still grant, and a setting that is not a map grants nothing at all.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T22-12-40Z.json: reader row 3 (alternatives) — "the size and review settings" are not introduced
findings.recommendation: Name them as orbit's size ceiling and review preference settings.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T23-31-55Z.json: reader row 3 (why) — "the rule that orbit never reads git state" is no ruling the reader can find, and what stops the run is unsaid
findings.recommendation: Say the stop comes from the review's own instructions (they refuse an uncommitted tree, so no record lands and the chain reports no progress), and that the engine's status reads no git state by design.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-09T23-31-55Z.json: reader row 1 (decided) — "a blind pair" is undefined
findings.recommendation: Define it or add it to defines.

commentary: Verification of the two walks over their sweep scopes. Seven of the eight resolved entries landed: the replaced-stop fix reads the chain's latest record and its test now proves both resolution forms; the tag test's closed inventory fails a new prompt carrying any valid tag; the no-change-target and decision-prompt sentences, the onboard qualification, the cli.md rows and the hash provenance notes are present. The dirty-tree entry regressed on one clause: its end-step sentence describes a paste fallback the launch route never takes, contradicting the handoff reference it summarizes, while the delta and the docs state it correctly — a mechanism claim written without reading the owner. The residual diff since the external return's commit lists only files inside the walks' edit records. The reader's twelve findings cluster on restatement: four records (17-50-53Z, 17-50-54Z, 18-10-03Z, and 22-12-40Z by its own detail) narrow or widen what they cite, and three lean on unintroduced terms (blind pair, launch note). The two records addressing "you" rather than "the user" (R-adf-10) fall outside the reader rows.
